## Choose an example

On **1. Data**, choose a **Packaged training example** to load it immediately. Use **Reload selected example** to restore it after an upload.
Provide one labeled dataset. On Features, Shiny divides it into training,
validation and test sets; no separate unlabeled file is required.
Loading or downloading data does not train a model. The app reads files from
the installed package, using `system.file("extdata", ..., package = "DDESONN")`.
Iris and mtcars come from R's datasets package. These choices work offline;
the GitHub source link is for browsing, not an automatic download fallback.

| Example | Suggested task / target | Starting predictors | Important context |
|---|---|---|---|
| Iris | Multiclass / Species | Four numeric measurements | Small first example, 150 rows. |
| mtcars | Regression / mpg | All columns except mpg | Small regression example, 32 rows. |
| Heart failure | Binary / DEATH_EVENT | All 12 numeric predictors | Repeated inputs limit evaluation; see the research vignette. |
| WMT prices | Regression / close | All columns except close | Packaged snapshot; ordered splitting is suggested. This same-row illustration is not a validated forecast. |
| Customer labeled dataset | Multiclass / Segmentation | All columns except Segmentation | Review ID, categories and missing values before preparation. |

The full original rows and columns remain available for inspection and download.
All columns except the target start selected. Preprocessing choices are shown explicitly before preparation. Review identifiers and information derived from the answer. Auto proposes
identifier exclusions, encoding and missing-value rules; inspect or override
the plan before preparing. The raw dataset is retained unchanged. For WMT, review the nonnumeric date and answer-derived adjusted close.
On Features, the dataset name confirms what is loaded. Both navigation paths
show its target and predictor defaults; moving between tabs preserves your edits.

## A first iris model

1. Keep Iris on Data; inspect its preview.
2. On **2. Features**, use target **Species**, the four measurement predictors,
   and **Multiclass classification**. Review the split and click **Prepare data**.
3. On **3. Build & Train**, keep **Basic**, try hidden-layer sizes `8` and
   **Epochs per model fit** `2`, then click **Train new model**.
4. On **4. Model / Results**, inspect the evaluations and predictions. Results
   depend on settings and seed; this is a small workflow example, not a performance claim.

For mtcars, load its example instead. The default target is mpg, task Regression, and predictors all other columns.
For a smaller example, manually select only wt and hp on Features.
**Show full R code** follows your actual prepared data and settings after preparation.

## Read the same data in R

```{r load-r-examples, eval=FALSE}
data <- datasets::iris
# Or use the regression example:
data <- datasets::mtcars
```

```{r load-package-csv, eval=FALSE}
path <- system.file("extdata", "heart_failure_clinical_records.csv",
                    package = "DDESONN")
stopifnot(nzchar(path))
data <- read.csv(path, check.names = FALSE)
```

The app's generated recipes use the corresponding installed filename and record
a SHA256 check for packaged CSVs, so changed data is detected when reproducing a
recipe. Original packaged CSV downloads preserve their bytes. Iris/mtcars CSV
exports contain the dataset columns; R row names are not exported as predictors.
The existing data files are reused; no external datasets are added by this change.

## Predict using the unlabeled customer file

Train a customer model first, or load your compatible saved workbench bundle.
The customer preset selects all non-target columns. Auto proposes excluding ID,
one-hot encoding the categories and handling missing predictor values. You can
therefore prepare the full relevant customer attributes without reducing them
to Age alone.
The matching prediction file provides the same predictor columns. Under **Model / Results → Saved models & predictions → Predict on new rows**,
click **Predict customer groups with completed model**, or download the optional
customer prediction CSV. These rows have no Segmentation labels; they are not
needed for the training, validation or test split. No pretrained
model is bundled or automatically loaded. The saved raw predictor names and types must match; fitted encoding, missing-value
rules and scaling are reused; incompatible data produces an error rather than
changing the trained model. For older numeric-only bundles, prediction inputs must still be complete numeric
values in the original schema.

Loading another dataset clears preparation for a new model while preserving
completed models. A raw file without target labels is not automatically assigned
a fake target. The original CSV upload and prediction-upload paths remain available.

## Seeds, evaluation and related guides

A seed value of 42 is not 42 runs. Basic uses the Features seed for one run.
Custom's training seed list repeats complete training runs on the same prepared
split: `42,43` with Single model and 100 epochs means two 100-epoch runs, 200 total.
Neither random nor ordered splitting automatically groups duplicate inputs or
related subjects. The heart-failure split correction remains separate future work.

The app's contextual links take you to **Vignettes** for this guide, the
standard-AdaGrad research record, single-run/ensemble plot controls and ensemble
logs. Installed HTML guides open locally when present; otherwise the links open
their online source. All guide navigation preserves your current session.

## Browse and profile the loaded data

The inspector follows the selected example or uploaded CSV. Choose first rows
(`head`), last rows (`tail`) or a starting row number, and show 1–100 rows at a
time. Choose visible columns to inspect wide files. The row count identifies the
subset and the full dataset size; the displayed R code reproduces that view.
These controls do not execute arbitrary R scripts or alter training inputs.

Open **Descriptive summary — full dataset** for types, distinct counts, missing
values and numeric means, standard deviations and quartiles across all rows.
Blank text counts as missing; infinite values are counted separately. Numeric
summaries and plots use finite values only, without cleaning the underlying data.
Open **Box-and-whisker plot** and choose a numeric column to explore its median,
spread and potential outliers. Columns use separate plots because units differ.

## Auto and Manual preprocessing

On Features, **Auto** suggests a complete plan using local, reproducible rules;
it does not call an AI service. Each section can follow the overall mode or use
an explicit choice. **Manual** starts with complete numeric inputs and asks you
to choose any required treatment. Standardization is independently controlled
by the existing training-means/SDs switch in either mode.

| Step | Auto | Other choices |
|---|---|---|
| Numeric missing/nonfinite values | Training median | Training mean, zero, or reject missing values |
| Unordered categories | One-hot encoding | Explicit ordinal order, or require numeric predictors |
| Missing categories | Separate Missing level | Most frequent training category, or reject missing values |
| Identifier-like names | Exclude ID, names ending `_id` or starting `id_` | Keep selected columns, or override a single column |

One-hot encoding gives categories separate 0/1 inputs without imposing an order.
For ordinal encoding, use **Override one column**, choose Ordinal, and enter an
explicit low-to-high order such as `Low|Average|High`. All training categories
must appear exactly once. Known levels become 1..K; missing uses 0 and unseen
uses -1. Choose ordinal encoding only when the order has a real meaning.
Click **Apply column override** to store it, or **Clear all column overrides**
to follow section rules again. The status lists overridden columns. Loading a
new dataset clears column overrides; merely moving between tabs preserves them.

The proposed table shows each selected column's type, role, encoding, missing
rule and reason. Identifier-name exclusions are suggestions, not proof of
irrelevance; review them and possible leakage. The Segmentation target keeps
its A/B/C/D labels and is never imputed. Missing target values cause an error.

Click Prepare data to split first, then fit category levels, replacement values
and standardization using **training rows only**. The fitted-rule disclosure
shows actual training replacements and category lists. No rows are removed.
Save the workbench bundle to retain the complete rules, output-column order,
model and training state. Validation, test and new prediction data reuse those
rules without recalculating medians, modes, levels or scaling.

A new one-hot category maps to a reserved Unknown input; missing categories
have a separate reserved input. Unknown inputs have no learned examples if
none existed during training, so predictions on new categories require care.
Blank text counts as missing; categorical whitespace is trimmed. Numeric
infinities are treated as missing. Entirely missing numeric training columns
need explicit zero filling or exclusion. A mode cannot be learned from an
entirely missing category; choose a Missing level instead.

Columns with more than 200 observed training categories, or a design exceeding
2,000 inputs, require explicit simplification. Dates and free text can require
manual conversion/exclusion; for the WMT illustration review the date column
and answer-derived adjusted close. Auto does not identify every leakage risk.

The preprocessing code preview records your choices. After preparation, the
full R code contains portable fitting and application functions and uses the
same split. All learned preprocessing precedes native Basic or Custom training;
the new preprocessing path disables additional internal input normalization.
Older numeric-only saved bundles remain supported without changing their rules.

## Read the defaults and training curves

A dropdown entry such as **Use Auto default: training median** means that this
step takes its treatment from Overall preprocessing. If you select Manual, the
inherited label changes to **Use Manual default: require complete**. Selecting
an explicit method such as Training mean overrides the overall choice and stays
selected when you switch modes. Per-column inheritance names the relevant step
above it. Click the info icon beside any preprocessing control to see what all
its options mean, plus a focused R example. Apply column override stores edits;
selecting a column alone does not apply them.

Custom runs may log multiple members, training seeds and MAIN/TEMP fits. A fresh
fit can start at a different loss, producing a sawtooth if those curves are
joined. The workbench now leaves fits unconnected, adds boundaries and labels,
and reports the local epoch on hover. Fit numbers follow log order; they do not
identify a specific seed, member or MAIN/TEMP role. Older Custom bundles lacking
fit metadata can infer boundaries from their configured epoch budget; the
chart explanation identifies this inference. Training loss is not held-out
performance or proof of a model-quality problem by itself.

Use Download PNG or SVG to save the chart, or Download loss data for the plotted
records including fit/local-epoch columns. Copy chart image puts the visible
chart bitmap on the clipboard in supported browsers. If browser permissions or
the RStudio viewer prevent image copying, use the PNG/SVG downloads instead.
